newsitem.title: USA: China blocks US chicken imports, USDA says.
newsitem.headline: China blocks US chicken imports, USDA says.

text.p: China has blocked imports of chicken meat from 10 U.S. states because of avian influenza concerns, Department of Agriculture Dairy, Livestock and Poultry Division Director John Reddington said Thursday.
Reddington said the U.S. agriculture attache in Beijing had confirmed that the ban was in effect by fax to Washington earlier Thursday.
He said Washington had instructed the attache to meet with Chinese authorities to discuss and try to resolve the situation but the earliest meeting that could be arranged was for Monday.
"Some of your shipments have been held up in Hong Kong, and there is nothing we can do about it until Monday," Reddington told U.S. broiler producers at a meeting outside Washington.
Reddington indicated he did not believe there was scientific merit to the stoppage.
"This ban doesn't make any sense, they're banning meat and not live birds," he said.
Reddington said there had been rumors last week that China would block imports of live U.S. birds, but Chinese officials visiting Washington reassured USDA that such a ban would not be implemented.
Richard Lobb, a spokesman for the U.S. National Broiler Council, said the industry was waiting for further guidance from the U.S. government before acting or calculating what the impact would be.
